title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Price Elasticity and Food Markets
description: This lesson quiz checks what you learned in the lesson. Submitting it meets the lesson's completion requirement (quiz submitted), and your score is recorded separately.

questions.prompt: A good's price elasticity of demand (absolute value) is 0.3. How would you describe its demand?
When the price rose from 4 to 6, quantity demanded fell from 120 to 80. Using the midpoint method, what is the elasticity (absolute value)? (Enter a decimal.)
If a seller raises the price of a good with inelastic demand, what happens to the seller's total revenue?

choices.text: Fewer units are sold, so total revenue falls as well
Quantity falls by a smaller percentage than price rises, so total revenue rises
Price and quantity change by the same percentage, so total revenue stays the same
The demand curve shifts right, so both quantity sold and total revenue rise

questions.prompt: In a market where food demand is inelastic, a bumper harvest sharply increases supply. What is a likely result?

choices.text: The price falls sharply, and farm total revenue may decrease
The price falls slightly, and farm total revenue rises sharply
More units are sold, so farm total revenue also rises
The demand curve shifts to the right, so the price rises

questions.prompt: Demand for a good is Q = 80 − 2P. At what price is total revenue (P × Q) the largest? (Enter a number only.)
